ranges.note: Two independently checked records concern the approximate Neolithic occupation phase at Koorkula Valgjarv and the first excavated settlement phase at Zurich Parkhaus Opera. The author made 47 queries across all nine working regions and retained 13 withheld or deferred tracks. Both retained records concern Europe; the other regions remain research gaps. Full ranges of 3300-3200 cal BC and 3234-3226 BC remain intact, without annual activity, continuous occupation or coverage of later years inferred from their endpoints. The reviewer confirmed both historical payloads and both substantive source records; two earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps.

Seven independently checked records concern Newgrange, the approximate foundation of Shahr-i Sokhta, monumental buildings at Uruk, shell-rich deposits at Ru Diep, occupation onset at Upanca, royal imagery at Nag el-Hamdulab and beads in a Kara-depe burial. Full approximate dates, contextual horizons, individual samples and occupation intervals remain distinct. Ru Diep and Upanca keep full ranges extending beyond this century; these establish neither activity in every year nor researched coverage of later centuries. Searches covered nine regions, but sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Oceania and many other areas have no retained event. Upanca retains earlier independently read table evidence; the follow-up access limitation and unverified author retrieval assertions remain explicit in the research note. Empty years remain research gaps.

Six independently checked records concern Egyptian political unification, the Stenness henge, high dams at Liangzhu, the approximate start of the Thach Lac sequence, early weighing objects, and a qualified cattle-husbandry interpretation north of the Black Sea. These are approximate archaeological attestations, constructions or processes; no strict single-calendar-year occurrence is established. Full date intervals, competing chronologies and later endpoints remain in single records. Their spans establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. The Americas, Oceania, South Asia, much of Africa and other regions remain gaps. Empty years are research gaps.

Six independently checked records concern a brewery at Abydos, the low dams and main city construction at Liangzhu, Stonehenge ditch and banks, a specific Valdivia stone figure, and one burial at Kerma. Full approximate dates and construction intervals remain qualified. Kerma retains a provisional prose estimate alongside the chronology table question mark; settlement samples do not date the grave. Caral, Nausharo, Kot Diji-Amri contacts, aggregated Afanasievo burials and access-limited Kobeba remain withheld. South Asia, Southeast Asia, Oceania, the steppe and much of Africa and the Americas remain gaps. Long intervals establish no occurrence in every year or researched coverage of later centuries. Empty years are research gaps.

Five independently checked records concern engraved stones deposited at Vasagard, Dholavira wall reinforcement, a particular Sumerian mace head, a qualified dietary interpretation at Narensu, and grave M118 at Liangwangcheng. Approximate dates, construction periods, object intervals and grave-phase dates remain distinct. Ashqelon abandonment is withheld because the published slash date does not establish the chosen continuous interval. No exact annual occurrence or first cultivation is established. Sub-Saharan Africa, the Americas, Southeast Asia, Oceania and most other areas remain gaps. Full intervals extending beyond this block establish no researched coverage of later centuries. Empty years remain research gaps.

Nine independently checked records concern two Ness of Brodgar building episodes, tentative Harappa perimeter walls, an inscribed Harappa rim sherd, a Linjia tin-bronze knife, three individually dated museum artifacts and initial construction of the Callacpuma circular plaza. Approximate dates and full archaeological or object ranges remain qualified; no exact annual occurrence, manufacturing locality or invented inscription reading is established. Al-Ghoryeen S3 is withheld because its slash date does not explicitly support the proposed continuous interval. The steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Later range endpoints do not establish researched coverage of subsequent centuries. Empty years remain research gaps.

Four independently checked historical records concern inferred winter millet foddering at Dali, mixed crop cultivation at Baodun, abandonment of older Kalibangan and covered storage pits on Sai. Approximate site dates, interpretive causes and full occupation ranges remain qualified. Baodun retains 2700-2000 BC and its earlier published 2700-2100 BC alternative; neither implies cultivation in every year or researched coverage of later centuries. Europe, sub-Saharan Africa, Southeast Asia, the Americas, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Prior author retrieval dates retain their separately unverified provenance status; the reviewer confirmed all four historical payloads and five substantive source metadata records. Empty years remain research gaps.
Annual research has not started in this catalog.

Nine independently checked records concern the central Stonehenge settings, the approximate creation of ancient Kerma, an Indus jar, a Shijiahe ornament, an attained settlement state at Real Alto, Silbury Hill construction, the probable millet diet of one Aigyrzhal individual, a Sahure statue and Eannatum's victory stele. All nine working regions were searched; Southeast Asia, Oceania and many other areas remain gaps. Approximate estimates, complete object and sample intervals, and commemorative claims remain distinct. The Aigyrzhal main article supports the event independently; its visually unverified supplement is withheld. Full ranges beyond the century establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. Empty years remain research gaps.

Two records retain the independently supported historical cores of a rounded room at La Galgada and the funerary texts in Unas's pyramid. The room date remains a qualified published estimate with no individually identified sample or confidence interval. Two competing reign chronologies remain explicit for Unas, without fixing a carving year. All nine working regions were searched through 63 queries; the final records concern the Americas and North Africa/Middle East, with seven regions and many areas still missing. The jade object and Ebla palace fire are withheld after independent access limitations. Earlier retrieval acts remain unestablished and editorial importance is assessed under the brief. Full date qualifications remain in single records. Empty years remain research gaps.

Three independently source-checked records concern the Enheduanna disc, the approximate emergence of Shimao as a political centre and Naram-Sin's victory stele. Competing reign chronologies and approximate object dates remain explicit; no exact foundation, battle or carving year is inferred. The author searched all nine working regions through 49 queries, retaining two Mesopotamian records and one East Asian record. Other regions remain gaps. Full date qualifications stay in single records and do not establish activity in each year. Earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps.

Three independently checked records concern Akkad’s fragmentation, domestic reuse at Edfu and a qualified climate framework for the Levant. Full competing or approximate intervals remain intact; their endpoints establish no continuous collapse, annual activity, universal drought or researched coverage of later centuries. The author made 30 discovery queries across nine working regions; all retained events concern the Middle East and North Africa, leaving the other eight regions as gaps. Tell Leilan and three object-based event selections remain withheld. Four earlier author retrieval assertions remain separately unverified. Empty years remain research gaps.

Eight independently source-checked records concern Dholavira infrastructure decline, Taosi urban enclosure, fortified Sintashta settlements, two Shulgi episodes, Mentuhotep II’s complex and reunification of Egypt, and Ur’s fall. The author logged 32 discovery queries across nine working regions; five retained events concern the Middle East and North Africa, with one each in East Asia, South Asia and the steppe and Central Asia. The other five regions remain gaps. Full phases, reign bounds and competing chronologies remain distinct; Sintashta placement is framework-dependent and Ur’s alternative dynasty endpoint does not independently date a conquest. Public summary, abstract and preview limits remain explicit. Empty years remain research gaps.

Sixteen independently checked records cover late Taosi destruction, Khok Phanom Di settlement, Malia palace construction, Gulf settlement changes, Egyptian campaigns and building programmes, Assyrian trade and four distinct Nippur or Isin developments. Full archaeological phases and competing reign chronologies remain intact. Bologna's earlier successful reading and its later access denial are recorded separately. Leubingen remains withheld because its scientific dating evidence was not accessible. Searches covered nine working regions; the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa, South Asia, Oceania and the steppe and Central Asia have no retained event. Empty years remain research gaps, and long intervals establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later centuries.
Annual research has not started in this catalog.

Twenty-seven independently checked records cover Roman political and military developments, maritime contacts, scientific and technical works, Chinese court changes and Buddhist translations, and Teotihuacan civic rebuilding. Four other candidates remain withheld, two for unresolved complete chronology and two for standalone-event significance. Full intervals and attributed chronologies remain explicit, including AD 101–200 and Kanishka 127/128. Searches covered nine regions; sub-Saharan Africa and Oceania have no retained event, and represented regions remain incomplete. Empty years remain research gaps, and later interval endpoints establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later centuries.

AD200 source review and bilingual subset: 17 events, 16 sources; 35 discovery queries across nine regions. Four regions have no retained event. Twelve original candidates are withheld, and all chronology qualifications remain explicit.

Twenty-nine independently source-checked records cover selected events in Europe, East Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, the Americas, sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia. Europe has nine records and East Asia eight; Roman imperial and ecclesiastical history dominates. Southeast Asia and Oceania have no retained event. The author logged 21 discovery queries across nine working regions. The Nasca bowl, Sri Lankan tooth-relic account, Pachomios baptism and My Son remain withheld. Puranas retain the full AD301-400 interval, and conflicting source dates remain explicit. Full intervals establish no annual occurrence or researched coverage of later years. Empty years and regions remain research gaps.
Annual research has not started in this catalog.

Nineteen independently checked records cover selected events in Europe, East Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Europe has nine records and East Asia five; the remaining represented regions have one each. The Middle East and North Africa and Oceania have no retained event. Rosalila is withheld because its dedication date and source metadata remain unestablished. Exact corrections preserve complete date intervals, source attribution and editorial importance limits. Earlier author retrieval assertions remain unverified. Empty years and regions remain research gaps.
Annual research has not started in this catalog.

Thirty-four independently checked events cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, sub-Saharan Africa, Central Asia, South Asia, East Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event. Europe has ten records; African coverage is limited to a broadly dated Wanar object, American coverage to Copan and Quirigua, and Southeast Asian coverage to Java. Full intervals and date qualifications remain intact. Two unsupported records are withheld, and earlier author retrieval assertions remain unestablished. Empty years and regions remain research gaps.

44 independently checked event records cover parts of Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event. Japan and court/religious history are overrepresented; much of Africa, maritime Southeast Asia, northern South Asia, the Americas and other regions need further work. Ife (circa 800–1000) and Igbo-Ukwu (disputed ninth- and tenth-century dates, numeric span 800–999) are single uncertain records whose spans cross the batch boundary. Their presence does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred.

44 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, southern Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas including Greenland. Oceania and Japan have no retained event; sub-Saharan Africa has only Schroda. Northern and eastern South Asia, maritime Southeast Asia, much of Africa and the Americas, and other regions need further research. Shanga and the proposed Kokinshu completion event are withheld because their submitted dates remain unresolved. Tula retains its full circa 900–1150 phase as one record; this does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred.

45 independently checked events cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, southern Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and the Americas. Oceania has no retained event; sub-Saharan Africa has only the approximate K2 phase. Iberia, Scandinavia beyond Cnut, Egyptian and South Arabian politics, western and central steppe, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bangladesh, the Philippines, much of Africa and the Americas require more research. Shanga and the proposed Ghana1076 conquest remain withheld. K2 retains its full approximate 1000–1220 phase once; that endpoint does not establish researched coverage of later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred.

56 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and the Caucasus, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Americas including Greenland, and Oceania. Oceania has only Nan Madol; sub-Saharan Africa has Timbuktu, Maryam Nazret and Soso. China and Japan dominate East Asia. Most African regions, the Andes and Caribbean, much of South Asia and maritime Southeast Asia remain gaps. Goryeo1170, Nalanda1193 and proposed exact Oceanian arrivals are withheld; other candidates such as Lalibela remain outside this batch. Maryam Nazret1101–1200, Nan Madol1180–1200 and Cliff Palace1190–1280 retain their complete uncertain or phased intervals once. Their endpoints do not establish researched later years. Empty years are research gaps, not evidence that no event occurred.

55 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and Caucasus, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Americas and Oceania. Warfare and changes of rulers dominate. Sub-Saharan Africa has only Mapungubwe, Sundiata and the Ethiopian dynastic change; Oceania has one explicitly modeled North Island settlement interval, not an exact arrival. Much of Africa and the Americas, Burma, Thailand, maritime Southeast Asia and other Pacific islands remain gaps, alongside economic, social, religious and natural history. Ram Khamhaeng and a separate Majapahit foundation date remain withheld; access gaps prevented proposed Xiangyang/Hangzhou additions. Mapungubwe1220–1290, the Khwarazm campaign1218–1224 and other phases remain single records. Empty years are research gaps.

62 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, the steppe and Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia and central Mexico. Oceania has no retained event. The strict sub-Saharan selection has Husuni Kubwa and two Ibn Battuta visits; Mansa Musa is counted at his Cairo visit. Most African and American regions, maritime Southeast Asia, science, technology, social history and environmental events need more research. Tenochtitlan retains an approximate foundation tradition distinct from earlier occupation; Tlatelolco and Acamapichtli retain competing chronologies. Luang Prabang dates capital status, not foundation. Long phases remain single records. Empty years are research gaps.

55 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Americas and Oceania. Europe and East Asia are overrepresented. Oceania has only an approximate Rangitoto eruption; the Americas concern Mexico and the Andes. Other regions, social history, science, technology and environmental history need further work. Source disagreements and full uncertainty intervals remain visible. Approximate dates and long processes do not establish an event in every year; empty years remain research gaps.

38 independently checked event records cover selected acts in Europe, the Middle East and North Africa, Central Asia, sub-Saharan Africa, East Asia, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Americas and Oceania. Europe and southern/eastern Asia are overrepresented. Sub-Saharan records concern Kongo and Ndongo; American records concern central Mexico. Oceania has three scoped records. Many regions, social history, science, technology and environmental history remain gaps. Approximate dates and the single source-supplied range preserve their limits; empty years remain research gaps. This batch ends at the maximum start year, 1530, and makes no whole-century completeness claim.
